claim_being_audited: The Actor recommends certifying the current model release on the basis that aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and certification can be defended if the current release documentation discloses the health-plan benefits support regression as a material limitation.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and to disclose material segment weaknesses unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation; the provided evidence does not show that this disclosure has actually been made.
The health-plan benefits support slice is below the warning threshold for a named use case, which is direct evidence of a current material limitation.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is not attached to reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language, so it cannot satisfy the policy predicate.
Prior approval from nine weeks earlier predates the current corpus refresh and eval batch and therefore cannot supply current-release coverage.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify the model now is not fully supported because no admissible evidence shows that the current model-card or release documentation already includes the required disclosure.
Any implication that post-launch monitoring can stand in for approved mitigation or current disclosure is unsupported by the record.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release documentation or model-card text showing the current evaluation batch and explicit disclosure of the health-plan benefits support regression.
If disclosure has not been made, provide an approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation covering this subgroup weakness before launch.
Provide the materiality determination or approval record, if one exists, showing why this subgroup regression is not treated as a blocking weakness for the named launch use case.
decision_criteria: If current release documentation already reflects the current eval results and explicitly discloses the subgroup regression, the verdict could move toward compliant_with_caveats.
If there is an approved pre-launch mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering this weakness, the certification basis would materially strengthen.
If neither disclosure nor approved mitigation exists, certification fails the stated policy threshold and the verdict would move to noncompliant.
